newsitem.title: POLAND: Volkswagen said mulling Polish investment.
newsitem.headline: Volkswagen said mulling Polish investment.

text.p: A Polish government official said Monday that representatives of the German Volkswagen group expressed interest in setting up a motor-car factory in the southwestern Polish province of Jelenia Gora.
The PAP news agency quoted provincial spokesman Janusz Rozlal as saying that representatives of Volkswagen had expressed these views when they visited Jelenia Gora.

"The Germans are interested in manufacturing facilities in the Len SA factory in Kamienna Gora, a furniture factory in Lubawka or facilities in a former pre-fab housing factory in Jelenia Gora," PAP news agency quoted Rozlal as saying.
It was not immediately clear whether Volkswagen was considering opening only a car-assembly plant using imported parts, a car-parts factory or a fully-fledged car factory. @
Volkswagen now has a car-assembly plant in the western town of Poznan, which assembles Volkswagen delivery vans and passenger models of Skoda, a Czech carmaker partly owned by Volkswagen.
The Poznan plant, in which Volkswagen has a 25.4 percent stake in Poznan, has a production capacity of 20,000 units annually.
